summary: AP firmware returns stale DHCP route options causing Windows fast-roam + WireGuard split-tunnel blackhole
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple employees on the SF office 5GHz SSID experienced intermittent inability to reach internal services (git.redwood, artifactory, internal vault) immediately after roaming between APs. Symptoms looked like successful VPN/WireGuard connection but TCP sessions to internal subnets failed.

Impact:
- Several engineers reported push/pull failures to git and timeouts to internal CI runners during active development.
- Incident affected ~8 users over an ~3 hour window on 2026-03-10.
- Impacted users were on Windows 11 laptops with the Redwood WireGuard split-tunnel profile.

Environment:
- Office SSID: Redwood-Corp (802.11ac wave2, 5GHz primary)
- AP vendor/firmware: EdgeAP (reported by AP console) 6.4.1-build-20260228
- VPN: WireGuard client managed by Redwood SSO profiles (split-tunnel: internal subnets routed via WG, internet via local gateway)
- DHCP: Cisco DHCP server handing options; APs are configured to proxy DHCP and inject option 121 (classless static route) for some downstream devices for legacy printers.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) User on laptop actively using git fetch/push on internal host.
2) Client roams between two nearby APs (fast-roam assisted by 802.11r/k).
3) Reassociation completes, DHCP probe/renew occurs (AP performs DHCP proxy behavior).
4) WireGuard remains connected but traffic to 10.10.0.0/16 (internal services) gets blackholed; routes appear to exist but ping/traceroute exits at the laptop.
5) Disconnecting WireGuard and reconnecting restores connectivity.
6) Some users only required a forced DHCP renew to resolve transiently.

Logs / snippets:
- Windows route table immediately after roam showed duplicate route to 10.10.0.0/16: one via WireGuard interface (metric 20) and another via gateway 192.168.1.1 (metric 5) installed as a classless static route from DHCP option 121.
- AP syslog (excerpt): "DHCP proxy: forwarded DHCP OFFER with option 121 to client ID 0x9f..."
- WireGuard kept the interface up; interface counters showed packets delivered but no L3 response.

Initial hypothesis:
The AP firmware (6.4.1) is incorrectly replaying a stale DHCP option 121 from a cached packet when acting as DHCP proxy during client reassociation. That option installs a more specific route for internal subnets into the OS route table with a lower metric than the WireGuard route, causing split-tunnel to send internal-bound traffic to the local gateway instead of the tunnel, producing a blackhole.

Why this is different from previous 'sticky route' reports:
- In contrast to INT-37421 which involved route binding during interface tear-down, this is a DHCP option injection at reassociation time where WireGuard did not drop the tunnel.
- Affects only clients which use split-tunnel (WireGuard) and the AP DHCP proxy path; full-tunnel clients unaffected.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Maya Chen: First report from user about git push failing after walking between desks. Captured Windows route table and WireGuard config.

2026-03-10 11:05 - NetOps (Ethan Rivera): Reproduced in lab by forcing roam with a lab laptop; saw option 121 injected by AP during DHCP renew. Confirmed route metrics prioritize local shim over WG route.

2026-03-10 12:20 - SRE (Priya Iyer): Tested on macOS and Linux — macOS respects metric and worked (no collision); Linux showed similar collision but preferred WG route because of metric ordering. Narrowly Windows-specific due to metric assignment behavior.
2026-03-10 13:00 - NetOps: Pulled AP logs and noticed identical DHCP proxy packet IDs being replayed for different clients (possible firmware reuse of cached packets).
2026-03-10 15:10 - Engineering (infra-srv): Verified WireGuard route persists during roam; kernel still had WG route but OS accepted new classless route with lower metric.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Vendor (EdgeAP) engaged via support ticket: EdgeAP confirmed a regression in DHCP proxy caching behavior in 6.4.1; recommended temporary AP config change to disable DHCP proxying per SSID.
2026-03-11 11:45 - NetOps: Rolled temporary AP config to disable DHCP proxy for Redwood-Corp SSID on two edge APs in SF and observed no recurrence in the small user group during 2-hour soak.
2026-03-12 08:20 - QA: Deployed firmware 6.4.2-beta (vendor-supplied) to lab AP and confirmed cache fix; option 121 no longer replayed during reassociation.
2026-03-13 09:00 - NetOps: Planned production firmware upgrade schedule and post-deploy monitoring; no further incidents reported since fix rollout.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10 10:20): I'm attaching the Windows route table and WireGuard wg0 config from affected laptop. Route shows 10.10.0.0/16 via 192.168.1.1 metric 5 and wg0 route metric 20.
Ethan Rivera (2026-03-10 11:10): Reproduced in lab. Short-term workaround: run 'ipconfig /renew' or disconnect/reconnect WireGuard. I will escalate to vendor for AP firmware behavior.
Priya Iyer (2026-03-10 12:30): Noting that macOS didn't exhibit the bug — Windows route metric handling appears to make this more visible. Marking as Sev1 because of developer impact.
EdgeAP Support (2026-03-11 09:05): We have a confirmed regression in 6.4.1 where DHCP proxy cache entries may be reused incorrectly. A firmware patch is in testing (6.4.2-beta).
Ethan Rivera (2026-03-11 11:50): Disabled DHCP proxy on SSID in two AP clusters in SF as a mitigation. Requesting SOC to monitor for related auth failures.
Maya Chen (2026-03-12 09:10): After mitigation I can no longer reproduce the problem. Thanks team.
Ethan Rivera (2026-03-13 09:05): Production rollout of EdgeAP 6.4.2 scheduled for 2026-03-13 23:00 PT with 30-minute canary. No incidents during staged rollout. Closing as Resolved.
resolution:
Workaround: Disable DHCP proxy (AP-level) for Redwood-Corp SSID on affected AP clusters and instruct Windows users to run 'ipconfig /renew' or toggle WireGuard connection if they hit the issue.
Permanent fix: Vendor firmware patch 6.4.2 which removes DHCP proxy cache reuse was applied in production. Post-deploy monitoring for 48 hours showed no recurrence.
Follow-up: Add a monitoring alert to detect duplicate classless static routes (option 121) appearing on endpoints and include a troubleshooting checklist in the WiFi-Roam runbook.
resolution_notes:
- Applied temporary AP config change 2026-03-11 11:45 PT.
- EdgeAP 6.4.2 rolled to SF cluster 2026-03-13 23:00 PT with 30m canary then full rollout.
- Added postmortem entry to Confluence and owner assigned for runbook update (Ethan Rivera).
